title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Elements in Array Distinct
statement: You are given an integer array `nums`. One operation deletes the first three elements of the array, or all of them when fewer than three are left. Return the fewest operations after which the elements still in the array are pairwise distinct. An empty array counts as distinct, so an answer always exists.
notes:
## Intuition

Every operation removes a prefix, so after `k` operations what is left is the suffix that starts at index `3k`. A suffix is distinct exactly when it starts after the last position whose value appears again further right. Scanning from the right with a set finds that position in one pass. The brute force would simulate the operations and recheck the remaining suffix for repeats after each one.

## Approach

1. Walk `i` from the last index down to 0, keeping the values to the right of `i` in `seen`.
2. The first `nums[i]` that is already in `seen` is the rightmost value that repeats. The remaining array must start after `i`, so at least `i + 1` elements have to go.
3. Each operation removes three, so return `Math.floor(i / 3) + 1`, which is ⌈(i + 1) / 3⌉.
4. If the scan ends without a repeat, the array is already distinct: return 0.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 3, 5, 7]`. Scanning from the right, `seen` collects 7, 5 and 3 at indices 8, 7 and 6. At `i = 5` the value 3 is already in `seen`, so the first six elements must go: `Math.floor(5 / 3) + 1 = 2` operations, which leave `[3, 5, 7]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time set operations.
- Space: O(n) for `seen`.

## Pitfalls

- The rightmost repeated position decides the answer, not the first duplicate pair seen from the left.
- Removing `i + 1` elements takes ⌈(i + 1) / 3⌉ operations; the last one may remove fewer than three.
- When nothing repeats, return 0 rather than counting an operation.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | the values to the right of index `i` |
| `i` | the current index, scanned from right to left |

narration.2: seen will hold every value to the right of the current index.
narration.3: Scan from the last index towards the front.
narration.4: Has this value already appeared further right?
narration.5: Yes: the remaining array must start after i, so i + 1 elements go, which takes floor(i / 3) + 1 operations of three.
narration.7: No repeat yet, so remember this value for the indices to its left.
narration.9: No value repeats, so the array is already distinct and needs no operation.
